technologies.name: Thin-Film Composite (TFC) Reverse Osmosis (RO)
technologies.mechanism: Steric size exclusion, solution-diffusion transport, and Donnan electrostatic ion repulsion
technologies.waterRecoveryRate: 33% - 50% (Permeate to Brine ratio 1:1 to 1:2 with modern permeate pump)
pros: Rejects dissolved ions, heavy metals, and nanoplastics down to 0.1 nanometers
Achieves 98.9%+ removal of toxic PFAS 'forever chemicals' (PFOA, PFOS, GenX)
Reduces municipal fluoride by 90-95% via Donnan electrostatic exclusion
Eliminates ionic and colloidal lead, cadmium, hexavalent chromium, and arsenic
cons: Strips beneficial dietary minerals (calcium, magnesium) producing acidic pH 5.8-6.4 unless remineralized
Discharges brine wastewater (1:1 to 1:3 ratio depending on feed pressure and permeate pump)
Requires 45+ PSI feed pressure or internal booster pump

technologies.name: Hollow-Fiber Ultrafiltration (UF) Membrane
technologies.mechanism: Steric size exclusion across asymmetric semi-permeable hollow fiber capillary pores
pros: Blocks 99.8% of microplastics, bacteria, cysts, and colloidal turbidity
Retains 100% of healthy dissolved calcium and magnesium (alkaline neutral pH ~7.4)
Zero wastewater generation and operates at standard household line pressure
cons: Cannot reject dissolved mineral salts or small ionic molecules (Fluoride rejection < 5%)
Limited dissolved PFAS reduction without secondary activated carbon stage
Does not lower Total Dissolved Solids (TDS)

technologies.name: Extruded Catalytic Solid Carbon Block + Ion-Exchange
technologies.mechanism: Physical adsorption on high specific surface area (>1000 m²/g) + ion-exchange zeolite chemisorption
pros: Unsurpassed catalytic reduction of chloramines, chlorine, pesticides, and organic VOCs
High-density NSF 53 blocks effectively capture PFAS (90%+) and lead via ion-exchange binders
Retains essential minerals, zero wastewater, and easy cartridge swap
cons: Virtually zero removal of municipal fluoride (requires specialized activated alumina)
Carbon pores saturate over time; risk of contaminant desorption breakthrough if overdue for change
Does not reduce overall TDS or dissolved heavy metalloids like arsenic

technologies.name: Micro-Porous Ceramic Candle with Granular Carbon Core
technologies.mechanism: Tortuous micro-capillary mechanical sieving with silver-impregnated bacteriostatic ceramic outer shell
pros: Operates without electricity or plumbing water pressure (emergency/off-grid ready)
Washable and cleanable ceramic exterior prolongs service life in turbid conditions
Stops bacteria, cysts, parasites, and microplastics above 0.5 microns
cons: Slow drip filtration rate (1 to 2 gallons per hour)
Standard carbon core has limited fluoride removal unless secondary alumina post-filters are installed
Subject to channeling through granular carbon core if air pockets form

technologies.name: Standard Gravity Pitcher Filter (Loose GAC Media)
technologies.mechanism: Loose granular activated carbon (GAC) + cation exchange resin bead gravity percolation
pros: Inexpensive initial purchase and highly portable countertop footprint
Improves aesthetic chlorine taste and municipal water odor
cons: 0% fluoride removal; completely ineffective against dissolved ions
Poor PFAS and heavy metal removal on basic models; prone to water channeling
Moist carbon granules can foster rapid bacterial biofilm colonization within 30-45 days

pfas.name: PFAS 'Forever Chemicals' (PFOA, PFOS, GenX)
pfas.healthRisks: Renal cell carcinoma, testicular cancer, ulcerative colitis, thyroid disease, immune suppression, and reduced vaccine antibody response.
pfas.criticalMechanism: Extremely stable carbon-fluorine bonds (C-F) resist chemical degradation. Sub-nanometer molecules require molecular-weight steric exclusion (RO) or strong surface hydrophobic binding (catalytic carbon).

lead.name: Lead (Pb²⁺ Ionic & Colloidal)
lead.regulatoryLimit: 0.0 ppb MCLG / 10.0 ppb Action Level (EPA LCRI 2024)
lead.healthRisks: Irreversible neurodevelopmental impairment in infants/children, loss of IQ points, ADHD, adult hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and chronic kidney dysfunction.
lead.criticalMechanism: Exhibits dual phases: soluble divalent ions (Pb²⁺) and particulate colloidal lead. RO rejects ionic lead via charge exclusion; block filters require specialized cation-exchange binders.

fluoride.name: Fluoride (F⁻ Anion)
fluoride.regulatoryLimit: 0.7 ppm Target / 2.0 ppm Secondary Standard / 4.0 ppm MCL
fluoride.healthRisks: Dental fluorosis (enamel mottling), skeletal fluorosis (joint stiffness, bone fragility), and potential neurodevelopmental effects at concentrations exceeding 1.5 mg/L (NTP 2024 Monograph).
fluoride.criticalMechanism: Small hydrated ionic radius (0.352 nm). Standard carbon filters cannot adsorb F⁻. High-efficiency removal requires RO Donnan electrostatic repulsion or chemisorption on activated alumina.

microplastics.name: Microplastics & Nanoplastics (< 1 µm down to 10 nm)
microplastics.regulatoryLimit: Emerging Contaminant (CA SB 1422 / EU REACH Restrictions)
microplastics.healthRisks: Cellular internalization, translocation into capillary bloodstream, vascular plaque inflammation, endocrine disruption from leached bisphenols and phthalates.
microplastics.criticalMechanism: Particulate polymer fragments. RO membrane (0.0001 µm) and UF membrane (0.01 µm) provide near-absolute physical barrier interception.

arsenic.name: Inorganic Arsenic (As(III) Arsenite & As(V) Arsenate)
arsenic.healthRisks: Known Group 1 human carcinogen: skin, bladder, and lung cancers; hyperkeratosis; vascular peripheral disease ('blackfoot disease').
arsenic.criticalMechanism: As(V) is negatively charged at drinking water pH and rejected effectively by RO (>96%). As(III) is non-ionized at neutral pH and passes through unless pre-chlorinated/oxidized to As(V).

chloramines.name: Chloramines & Disinfection Byproducts (DBPs/THMs)
chloramines.healthRisks: Respiratory irritation, asthma exacerbation, formation of cytotoxic trihalomethanes (chloroform) and haloacetic acids.
chloramines.criticalMechanism: More chemically stable and persistent than free chlorine. Degrades standard RO polyamide membranes unless intercepted by an upstream catalytic activated carbon pre-filter.

nitrates.name: Nitrates & Nitrites (NO₃⁻ / NO₂⁻)
nitrates.healthRisks: Methemoglobinemia ('Blue Baby Syndrome') in infants under 6 months; suspected risk factor for colorectal cancers and thyroid goiter.
nitrates.criticalMechanism: Highly soluble monovalent anion. Requires high-rejection polyamide RO membranes or selective strong-base anion exchange resins.

tds.name: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS)
tds.healthRisks: High TDS indicates heavy mineral loading, hardness scaling, and possible industrial/agricultural ionic contaminants. Ultra-low TDS (< 30 ppm) indicates demineralized, corrosive water.
tds.criticalMechanism: Aggregate measure of all dissolved inorganic cations (Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Na⁺, K⁺) and anions (Cl⁻, SO₄²⁻, HCO₃⁻). RO is the only primary point-of-use technology that strips TDS by 90-98%.

waterSources.name: Standard Municipal City Tap Water
waterSources.description: Treated surface or blended aquifer water. Moderately hard, fluoridated at 0.7 ppm, disinfected with chloramines.

waterSources.name: City Tap with Aging Lead Service Lines
waterSources.description: Older urban distribution networks with pre-1986 lead utility supply lines or galvanized plumbing with lead solder.

waterSources.name: Private Groundwater Well (Hard / Agricultural Basin)
waterSources.description: Deep aquifer water with very high mineral hardness, elevated calcium/magnesium scaling potential, zero added chlorine/fluoride, but possible nitrates and arsenic.

waterSources.name: Surface Water Near Industrial / Military Airfield (PFAS Hotspot)
waterSources.description: Watersheds impacted by AFFF firefighting foam discharge, fluorochemical industrial manufacturing, or commercial airports.

remineralizationGuides.notes: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), long-term consumption of demineralized water (< 50 ppm TDS) lacks essential dietary magnesium and calcium, exerts higher osmotic load on intestinal mucous membranes, and can leech minerals from food during boiling.

Passing pure RO water through a secondary food-grade Calcite (calcium carbonate) and Corosex (magnesium oxide) cartridge restores non-corrosive pH, provides 15-20% of daily recommended hydration magnesium, and enhances crisp, natural palate taste.
